Neighbourhood specificity of ortholog pairs

Source: R/specificity.R
compare_specificity.Rd

Ranks each ortholog pair against every other gene of the partner species. This is the engine of method = "rank" in find_coexpressologs() and density_sweep(). summarize_specificity() turns its p-values into q-values.

Usage

compare_specificity(
  net1,
  net2,
  orthologs,
  n_cores = 1L,
  directions = c("both", "1to2", "2to1")
)

Arguments

net1

Network object for species 1 (output of compute_network()).

net2

Network object for species 2 (output of compute_network()).

orthologs

Data frame with columns gene1, gene2, and hog (output of prepare_orthologs()).

n_cores

Number of threads for parallel computation (default 1).

directions

"both" (default), "1to2" (anchors in species 1) or "2to1".

Value

A data frame with gene1, gene2, hog and, per requested direction (species1. for 1 to 2, species2. for 2 to 1):

neigh

Anchor degree.

mapped

Size of the translated set \(T\).

auroc

AUROC of \(T\) in the paired ortholog's ranking.

p_value

Rank p-value of the paired ortholog, as above.

jaccard

As in compare_neighborhoods().

n.cand

Number of candidate genes in the partner network.

effect_size

Equal to auroc.

auroc.grid

Matrix, one row per pair and one column per raw-p fraction f (1e-5 to 1, the column names): the ceiling(f * n.cand)-th largest candidate AUROC for the anchor, i.e. the AUROC the ortholog needs to reach raw p of about f. summarize_specificity() reads it for the edge power. It is computed on every call; a comparison against a null_network() partner, which only needs p_value, pays for it too (the package's own null runs skip it).

auroc and p_value are NA when \(T\) is empty or spans every other partner gene.

Details

The anchor's co-expression partners are translated to the partner species. The paired ortholog is scored by how well its own co-expression ranking recognises that translated list, compared with how well every other partner-species gene recognises it. The score follows the co-expression conservation score of Suresh et al. (2023). For anchor gene \(i\) in species 1 and direction 1 to 2:

  1. \(T\) is the set of species-2 genes orthologous, through any copy, to a network neighbour of \(i\) (an entry at or above the analysis threshold), minus every species-2 gene in \(i\)'s own ortholog group. Removing the own group keeps a pair from scoring itself through its paralogs.

  2. For every species-2 gene \(j\), the AUROC of \(T\) (without \(j\)) among the other \(n_2 - 1\) genes, ranked by their co-expression with \(j\). Stored entries of column \(j\) are ranked exactly; unstored entries tie at the bottom with their mid-rank. A sparse network therefore ranks only its stored top entries, so store_density sets the resolution.

  3. The p-value of the ortholog pair \((i, o)\) is \((1 + g) / n_2\), where \(g\) counts the genes \(j \ne o\) whose AUROC is at least that of \(o\): the rank of the ortholog among all species-2 genes. A translated list that thousands of genes recognise as well as \(o\) gives a large p-value however high its AUROC.

Direction 2 to 1 swaps the roles. All p-values of one direction lie on the same \(1 / n_2\) grid. They are not calibrated on their own: pass them with the p-values of a comparison against null_network() to summarize_specificity().

Runs on the sparse representation; dense networks are converted with every nonzero entry stored.

References

Suresh, H., Crow, M., Jorstad, N., Hodge, R., Lein, E., Dobin, A., Bakken, T. & Gillis, J. (2023). Comparative single-cell transcriptomic analysis of primate brains highlights human-specific regulatory evolution. Nature Ecology & Evolution, 7(11), 1930–1943. doi:10.1038/s41559-023-02186-7
